description: Write an e-invoice from structured data and check it: XRechnung 3.0 (UBL or CII), Peppol BIS Billing 3.0, ZUGFeRD / Factur-X EN 16931, a French CTC invoice, the Dutch NLCIUS / SI-UBL 2.0 (UBL or CII), Poland's KSeF FA(3) (the seller's NIP; another currency than PLN needs exchangeRate, PLN for one unit; prepaid needs prepaidDate) or Italy's FatturaPA 1.2 (buyer.recipientCode, the SdI code, or buyer.pec; an Italian buyer's codice fiscale as buyer.taxNumber; seller.taxRegime, RF19 for the flat-rate scheme) or Spain's Facturae 3.2.2 (the seller's and a Spanish buyer's NIF as vatId or taxNumber; a public administration buyer, NIF P, Q or S, needs buyer.dir3 {accounting, managing, processing}; euros only; prepaid needs prepaidDate; unsigned, the user signs it for FACe) or Slovenia's e-SLOG 2.0 (the seller's and the buyer's tax number as taxNumber or a Slovenian vatId; no attachments), with xmlvalid's e-invoice generator, then validated against the profile's schema and business rules. Pass `invoice` with `profile` (xrechnung, peppol, zugferd, france, nlcius, ksef, fatturapa, facturae, eslog), `lines` (name, quantity, unit, price, category, rate) and what the invoice needs: number, issueDate, dueDate, currency, buyerReference (the Leitweg-ID for German public buyers), seller and buyer (name, street, city, postcode, country, vatId, endpoint {scheme, id}; seller.contact {name, phone, email}), payment (means, iban, bic). Amounts are worked out in decimal. Returns the validation (result with errors and warnings), `invoice` (the totals as written and `ignored`, fields that were not taken) and `xml`, the written invoice, to give the user or fix and write again. Counts as one API validation of the account's monthly quota.

invoice.description: The invoice in the e-invoice generator's fields, as POST /api/v1/invoices takes it (https://xmlvalid.com/docs/api#invoices): profile (xrechnung, peppol, zugferd, france, nlcius, ksef, fatturapa, facturae, eslog), syntax (ubl or cii), type (380 invoice, 381 credit note), number, issueDate, dueDate, currency, exchangeRate (KSeF), buyerReference, orderReference, precedingInvoice, precedingDate, precedingKsefNumber (KSeF), note, paymentTerms, delivery {date, start, end}, seller {name, street, city, postcode, country, vatId, taxNumber, registration, taxRegime, endpoint {scheme, id}, contact {name, phone, email}}, buyer {name, street, city, postcode, country, vatId, taxNumber, recipientCode, pec, dir3 {accounting, managing, processing} (Facturae), endpoint}, payment {means, iban, bic, accountName, reference}, lines [{name, description, quantity, unit, price, category, rate, itemId}], charges [{charge, reason, amount, category, rate}], prepaid, prepaidDate (KSeF, Facturae). Numbers may be numbers or decimal strings.
